newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank targets high value customers.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank targets high value customers.

text.p: A new telephone system rolled out by NationsBank identifies customers who give it more business than others, and could mean they will spend less time on hold, a spokesman said Monday.

"In that new banking configuration... we can identify customers who have multiple relations with NationsBank," said spokesman Ellison Clary. "We can identify those customers with this new system and we can make sure they get service even faster than the other customers."

With the new system, callers to the bank's telephone system will punch in their account numbers, and then be divided into different electronic queues, depending on how much business they do with NationsBank.

For example, a customer who has a checking account, mortgage and credit cards with the Charlotte, North Carolina-based company would be divided from those customers who have only checking accounts, producing less revenue for the giant company.

The system, which was launched in Tallahassee and other sections of northern Florida, has been treated in local news reports as a way that banks favor so-called "high value" customers at the expense of others.
The bank spokesman said such reports were misinterpretations and that a longer wait faced by lower-revenue customers was intended to be no longer than 30 seconds.
"Nobody's going to have to hold forever," he said.
